solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Aunt Sally? Aunt Sally!

definitions.meaning: an Aunt Sally is a fairground throwing game where players hurl sticks at a dummy head
figuratively, an Aunt Sally is any target set up for abuse, criticism or blame

explanation.surface: The same name repeated, first as a puzzled question and then as an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a traditional English pub and fairground game of knocking a dummy's head off a post. The question mark points to the literal game, the exclamation to the figurative target.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a game played at a fair, and a legitimate target for attack or ridicule.

clue.text: Remnant found by lawman in ward

indicators.note: in says the lawman's letters sit inside the word for ward

parts.note: to ward off is to fend off
AG is the Attorney General, the chief law officer

explanation.surface: Leftover evidence discovered by a policeman in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ward' looks like a hospital room but is the verb, as in ward off. The lawman is not a policeman but AG, the Attorney General.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarette stub, or any last worthless scrap of something, is a remnant left over.

clue.text: Spotted in Arctic — a russet waxwing?

indicators.note: Spotted in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's note of a reddish waxwing glimpsed in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: The waxwing is a real bird, but the question mark flags a pun: the mythical flyer whose wings were made of feathers and wax.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Daedalus built his son wings of feathers held by wax, so he is literally a wax-winged figure.

clue.text: Hooted 'Humbug!' to one being married

parts.note: guff is empty talk, nonsense, humbug
A is the indefinite article, meaning one
wed means married

explanation.surface: Someone scoffed 'Humbug!' at a person getting married.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoot with laughter is to laugh loudly and boisterously, as one does in a belly laugh.

clue.text: He's lacking polish!

parts.note: a dull, non-glossy finish has no polish, and the 'He' points to a short boy's name spelt the same way

explanation.surface: A complaint about some man's lack of refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: The word describes an unshiny paint finish, and is also a man's name, hence 'He'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull, non-glossy surface finish lacks shine, and the name Matt makes it a person.

clue.text: Failure of firm following timeless injunctions

indicators.note: following places the firm's letters after the other piece
timeless means the letter standing for time is dropped from the word for injunctions

parts.note: fiats are authoritative orders or decrees
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company collapses after a stream of orders that never end.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the usual abbreviation for time, so 'timeless' strips it from FIATS, leaving FIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete and humiliating failure, a disaster or debacle, is a classic synonym.

clue.text: Damascenes, for example, slaying ceaselessly and indiscriminately

indicators.note: indiscriminately suggests the remaining letters are jumbled without order
ceaselessly means without its end, so the final letter of slaying goes

explanation.surface: Someone killing without pause and without discrimination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damascenes' look like people from Damascus but are damascened metalwork: designs of gold or silver set into steel. 'Ceaselessly' cuts the final G, leaving SLAYIN to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascening is decorative metal set into a surface, so damascenes are examples of inlaid work.

clue.text: Reliable member of film crew?

parts.note: a dependable chap is called reliable, and the film-crew member who records audio has a title saying exactly that

explanation.surface: Asking who on a film shoot can be depended upon.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words it means a reliable fellow; joined it is the crew member who handles recording.
explanation.definitionFit: The technician who records audio on a film set is the crew's recordist, called by this title.

clue.text: Come upon Miss Lynn hugging tenor in topless prank

indicators.note: in puts that whole group inside the trimmed prank
topless means the first letter of the word for prank is removed

parts.note: a joke is a prank

indicators.note: hugging means the singer's name wraps round the tenor

parts.note: Dame Vera Lynn was the wartime singer, the Forces' Sweetheart
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: A tenor in a cheeky prank involving the wartime singer Vera Lynn.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Vera Lynn was Britain's wartime 'Forces' Sweetheart'. 'Come upon' means befall, as misfortune overtakes a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtake is to come upon suddenly, as night or misfortune may befall someone.

clue.text: Writing on the wall for fat GI — exercise!

indicators.note: exercise suggests putting the letters through a workout so they move about

explanation.surface: A wall sign telling an overweight soldier to get some exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writing on the wall' sounds like the idiom for impending doom, but it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the singular of the Italian word for scrawled or painted wall inscriptions.

clue.text: Judge in drink becomes intimate

indicators.note: in puts the judge inside the drink

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink
Lud is from m'lud, how a judge is addressed in court

explanation.surface: A judge who has been drinking turns overly familiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' is a verb here, meaning hint, not an adjective meaning close.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate something is to hint at or suggest it indirectly, to refer to it obliquely.

clue.text: Using wrong remedy with splitting head — that's purgatory

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: a split-off head means the first letter of the word for remedy is lost

parts.note: a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: Taking the wrong medicine while suffering a splitting headache is agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splitting head' suggests a headache, but it means the head letter is split away.
explanation.definitionFit: Purgatory used loosely means great suffering or agony, a state of torment.

clue.text: Candy, periodically in vogue, takes centre stage in comeback

indicators.note: periodically takes every other letter of the following words
in comeback means the middle letters are read backwards
centre keeps only the middle letters of the word stage

explanation.surface: A sweet is fashionable again and makes a starring comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' gives N, O, U; 'centre' leaves TAG from STAGE and 'in comeback' turns it to GAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy confection of sugar or honey with nuts is a type of sweet, candy in American usage.

clue.text: Detective, you've a 'Morse' expression! Correct

parts.note: a cop is a police officer or detective
ye is an old form of you
dit is the spoken name for a Morse code dot

explanation.surface: Someone tells Inspector Morse he is wearing a typical Morse face.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse is the TV detective, but here it is the code; dits and dahs are how the dots and dashes are spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: To subedit is to correct a text for publication, which is what this editing task means.

clue.text: Involve brother in tree climbing

indicators.note: in places the brother inside the reversed tree
in a down clue climbing means the word for tree is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the lime is a tree, the linden

explanation.surface: A sibling gets caught up in a tree while climbing it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' reads upwards, so the tree appears backwards as EMIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to drag them into a conflict, to involve them deeply.

clue.text: Offer matador contract extension

indicators.note: contract means shrink the words, trimming them down to the run inside

explanation.surface: A bullfighter is offered a longer contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' reads as a noun about the matador's deal but is a verb telling you to shorten the words.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a pause sign extends a note beyond its written length, so it is a prolongation.

clue.text: Vessel 'casing' bay?

definitions.meaning: a barque, also spelt this way, is a sailing ship
the tough outer covering of a tree trunk
to bay is to howl as a hound does

explanation.surface: A boat surrounding a bay of water, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings: a sailing ship, a tree's outer skin, and a dog's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship, a tree's protective layer and a hound's cry all share this one spelling.

clue.text: Dopey ogles Mrs Batty

indicators.note: batty means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gormless chap leers at a dotty married woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Batty looks like a surname for Mrs, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopey means stupid and lacking sense, a near synonym of this northern English word.

clue.text: Head confiscates cushions

parts.note: bean is slang for the head
bags means seizes or takes possession of

explanation.surface: A head teacher seizes pupils' cushions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' reads as a head teacher but is slang for the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: Large bags filled with beads or beans serve as floor cushions or soft seats.

clue.text: Keep to main entree — toxin within not likely to cause harm

indicators.note: within says the answer lies inside the run of words before it

explanation.surface: Advice to stick to the main course, since any toxin there is harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Within' does double duty: it signals the hidden word and joins the definition, since these compounds are not actually the cause of food poisoning they were blamed for.
explanation.definitionFit: These are compounds formed in decaying protein, once wrongly blamed for food poisoning.

clue.text: Spell 'blooming flower'

parts.note: a blooming flower has opened
sesame is a flowering plant grown for its seeds

explanation.surface: Asking how to spell the phrase 'blooming flower'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like an instruction to spell a word, but it is a noun: a magic phrase, as in Ali Baba.
explanation.definitionFit: The magic words that open the robbers' cave in Ali Baba are the archetypal magic incantation.

clue.text: Damaged patrol car left centre deficient, relatively

indicators.note: damaged means the letters are knocked out of shape
deficient means these letters are missing from the patrol car

parts.note: L is short for left and C for centre

explanation.surface: A damaged police car's left-hand central section is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre' is not a pick of middle letters here: it is C, the abbreviation, alongside L for left; 'deficient' says both are missing before 'Damaged' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for in proportion: shares assigned in proportion are allocated relatively.

clue.text: Elderly portrayer of skilled felines and marsupial?

definitions.text: Elderly portrayer of skilled felines and marsupial?

parts.words: Elderly portrayer of skilled felines and marsupial?
parts.note: T.S. Eliot wrote the book of Practical Cats under an old pet name, and that name is also an Australasian tree-dwelling animal

explanation.surface: Someone who once depicted clever cats, and also an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliot's 'Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats' (the basis of the musical Cats) is the source: elderly is old, skilled felines are practical cats.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both Eliot's nickname for himself and a tree-dwelling pouched animal of Australia.

clue.text: PA's device reduced hassle for Emperor

indicators.note: reduced means the last letter is trimmed from the word for the device

parts.note: a mike is the microphone of a public address system
ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A personal assistant's gadget, cut back to reduce hassle for an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: PA reads as a personal assistant but means public address.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the historical title used in the West for the Emperor of Japan.

clue.text: Fool around among Japanese trees

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone clowning about in a Japanese garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool around' looks like one phrase, but 'Fool' is the definition and 'around' rearranges J (Japanese) with TREES.
explanation.definitionFit: A court jester was the professional fool who entertained a royal household.

clue.text: Strings are attached to this chap's endless shelling-out

parts.note: man means a chap

indicators.note: endless removes the last letter of the word for shelling out

parts.note: doling out is paying out, shelling out

explanation.surface: A man whose generosity always comes with conditions attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strings attached' suggests conditions, but it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: This lute-family instrument has paired metal strings fixed along its neck.

clue.text: Mediate Unionist politician's fury

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
ire is anger, fury

explanation.surface: A Unionist MP's anger needs calming by mediation.
explanation.definitionFit: To referee or arbitrate between parties is to mediate their dispute.

clue.text: Skirt edges of Utrecht during heart of season

indicators.note: during puts those edge letters inside the season's heart
heart of keeps only the middle two letters of the season, dropping the outer ones

parts.note: autumn is one of the four seasons

indicators.note: edges of takes the first and last letters of Utrecht

explanation.surface: Skirting the edge of Utrecht in the middle of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' looks like a verb meaning go round the edges, but it is the definition; the season must be found, and only autumn has a heart that fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina's short stiff frilled garment is a type of skirt.

clue.text: Go by stages into heart of Greece

indicators.note: into puts the stages inside those middle letters
heart of takes the middle letters of Greece

parts.note: laps are stages of a race

explanation.surface: Travelling in stages into central Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go by' is time passing, not travelling, despite the journey in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: When time goes by, it passes or slips away, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Very happy until jab festers

indicators.note: festers means the letters go bad and break down into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted right up until their injection goes septic.
explanation.definitionFit: Being triumphantly joyful, exultant, is being very happy.

clue.text: See 20
Entries in Telegraph Toughie's Friday number can be so long!

definitions.text: Entries in Telegraph Toughie's Friday number can be so long!

parts.words: Entries in Telegraph Toughie's Friday number can be so long!
parts.note: the initials of Telegraph, Toughie, Friday and number spell TTFN, ta-ta for now, a farewell

explanation.surface: A complaint that the answers in the Friday Toughie are very long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entries' are the first letters, TTFN: 'ta-ta for now', a British farewell popularised by radio host Jimmy Young. 'So long' is not about length but a goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: The French farewell, literally until we see again, means goodbye for now.
